reasoning: Over the last 45 days, there is only one general‑election, Louisiana‑specific Senate poll in the field: a Public Policy Polling survey for the Democratic Jamie Davis campaign showing Republican Julia Letlow leading by 4 points, 41%–37%, among registered voters, with 22% undecided.[2][5] No Louisiana‑specific 2026 presidential general‑election polling appears in the recent coverage or polling aggregators, so the best current quantitative snapshot is that the 2026 Senate race stands at roughly **R+4** in polling, against a structurally **R+11** environment per Cook PVI.[7] Other recent sources focus on the June 2026 Republican Senate runoff (Letlow vs. Fleming) and primary results rather than the current Davis–Letlow general election, so they are context rather than direct measures of the present margin.[1][8][15]

sources.name: Bayou Progressive (reporting Public Policy Polling toplines)
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey commissioned by the Jamie Davis campaign of 518 registered Louisiana voters found Republican Julia Letlow at 41% and Democrat Jamie Davis at 37%, with 22% undecided, i.e., Letlow +4.

sources.name: PredictionEdge (poll aggregation profile for Jamie Davis)
sources.details: Race profile and odds page summarizes the same Public Policy Polling survey as Letlow 41% vs. Davis 37%, listing the spread as Letlow +4.0 and treating it as the current polling baseline.

sources.name: New York Times – Louisiana U.S. Senate Election 2026: Latest Polls
sources.details: NYT polling page for the Louisiana U.S. Senate election lists several late‑June runoff‑stage polls of Republican candidates Julia Letlow and John Fleming (e.g., Letlow +3, Fleming +4, Fleming +5) that show a close GOP internal contest but do not test the current Letlow–Davis general election.

sources.name: WBRZ – Political analyst expects tight race for Senate runoff
sources.details: Local coverage of the June 27 Republican Senate runoff notes mixed internal polling, including a JMC Analytics survey commissioned by John Fleming showing Fleming up 6 and a Quantus Insights poll showing Letlow ahead 51.5%–48.5% on a two‑way ballot, illustrating a tight GOP runoff but not the current general election.

sources.name: NBC News – Louisiana Senate Primary Runoff Election 2026 Results
sources.details: NBC News runoff results article reports Julia Letlow winning the Republican Senate primary runoff with 56.9% to John Fleming’s 43.1%, and Jamie Davis winning the Democratic primary with 79.9% in his runoff, establishing the current general‑election matchup but not a margin between them.

sources.name: New York Times – Louisiana U.S. Senate Election 2026: BDPC early GOP matchup polling
sources.details: NYT polling page lists earlier BDPC polls of GOP figures (e.g., Letlow vs. Cassidy, Letlow vs. Fleming) with large Letlow leads, relevant to candidate strength but not directly measuring the current Letlow–Davis general election.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – PVI Map and State List
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s updated PVI materials and summary show Louisiana’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index as R+11, indicating the state voted 11 points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections.
